question: On one fixed public order-251 subgroup over F_1019, how do native Montgomery, short-Weierstrass, two-isogeny quotient, twisted-Edwards, bilinear-auxiliary, and affine-with-slope polynomial presentations differ in explicit input degree, regularity diagnostics, and completed shared-F4 solving degree when the represented factor-base points and planted relation are fixed?

claims.text: Every retained positive system accepts the planted relation, the negative Montgomery system is inconsistent, the A/A observations are identical, the degree-two map commutes on all 251 subgroup scalars, and the independently formed norm equals h_3^4.
The square-free quotient-w arm and the source Montgomery-u arm have the same measured degree profile on the fixed fixture; the isogeny removes fibre duplication rather than the intrinsic f_3 degree.
claims.if_supported: report exact equality of the preregistered degree tuple and keep the claim at this fixture
claims.if_not_supported: report every differing field and do not attribute a degree reduction or equality to the isogeny

claims.text: Retaining the raw norm h_3^4 changes total solving degree relative to square-free h_3 while preserving the exact zero set and affine leading-ideal regularity index.
claims.if_supported: report the signed total-degree delta as multiplicity overhead on this fixture
claims.if_not_supported: report which radical, regularity, completion, or degree control failed

claims.text: The Edwards bilinear-auxiliary presentation lowers maximum input degree relative to Edwards y-only without necessarily lowering completed total solving degree or selected F4 pair rows.
claims.if_supported: report input-degree, variable-count, total-degree, matrix, and pair-row deltas together
claims.if_not_supported: report the exact native-F4 deltas without importing the prior standalone-engine pair count

claims.text: Montgomery affine-with-slope has lower completed total solving degree than Montgomery u-only on the fixed fixture, at the cost of more variables and equations.
claims.if_supported: report the degree reduction beside variable, equation, matrix, and field-operation increases
claims.if_not_supported: report the exact completed comparison without a lowest-degree claim

claims.text: The short-Weierstrass x-only arm has the same measured degree profile as Montgomery u-only on the fixed fixture.
claims.if_supported: report exact equality of the preregistered degree tuple
claims.if_not_supported: report every differing field and retain a model-specific result

claims.text: Hessian is excluded because the fixed curve order 1004 is not divisible by three; Curve25519-scale transfer, complete index-calculus cost, external-CAS agreement, and any Coppersmith or integer-lifting claim are outside this qualification run.

arms.description: Native Montgomery x-only third summation polynomial with the two-element coordinate factor base.
Byte-identical Montgomery-u equations under a distinct observation identifier.
Native short-Weierstrass x-only third summation polynomial after the exact cubic translation.
Montgomery affine curve, chord-slope, target-x, and target-y equations with an explicit lambda auxiliary.
Square-free h_3 in w=u+1/u, represented as the ordinary f_3 on the degree-two isogenous destination U=w+A.
Unsquare-free raw norm h_3^4 retained exactly to isolate multiplicity overhead.
Native twisted-Edwards y-only third summation polynomial.
Twisted-Edwards affine addition with t_i=x_i*y_i and q=t_1*t_2 auxiliaries so every supplied equation is quadratic.
Montgomery-u system with target [37]G; exhaustive factor-base evaluation establishes no solution before F4.

positive.not_applicable_reason: Every nonnegative arm carries the same explicit planted solution and must pass expected_outcome_passed; a distinct positive arm would duplicate that detector path.

null_population.description: All four ordered pairs from the two fixed factor-base coordinate roots against target [37]G.
null_population.generator: Exhaustive Cartesian product of the two recorded Montgomery coordinate roots; no randomness or resampling.
null_population.why_n: The finite factor-base constraint splits completely into exactly two roots, so four ordered coordinate pairs exhaust the system's possible root assignments.

factors.name: field and source curve
factors.how: The exact fixture record and full UID are frozen in fixture.json.

factors.name: subgroup and relation
factors.how: Every positive arm transports the same two factor points and target through exact maps.

factors.name: represented factor base
factors.value: two negation orbits represented by two coordinate roots
factors.how: Coordinate membership polynomials are transported from the same source subgroup points.

factors.name: solver
factors.how: One pinned binary invokes every arm sequentially with the same F4 options.

factors.name: execution order
factors.how: The output contains exact counts only; local wall time is discarded and the A/A arm detects order-sensitive counted state.

factors.name: host
factors.how: Host and compiler facts are retained for replay provenance but cannot affect an admitted exact degree or counted F4 event.

transfer_obligations.scope: degree-two isogeny from the source Montgomery curve to the quotient destination
required_before_comparison: exact source and destination EC1 identities
gcd of map degree with subgroup order
map commutation on all retained subgroup scalars
no claim that an isogeny is a birational coordinate change

randomization.arm_order_reason: The study is one deterministic exact-computation panel with no admitted clock; fixed order is required for the byte-identical A/A count check.

seed_derivation.note: The instrument uses no randomness; zero is an export-shape placeholder and does not enter polynomial generation or F4.

instance_sampling.rule: The sole instance is the exact fixture in fixture.json; no curve, target, factor-base, or seed search occurs.

blinding.how: The systems and prior standalone-engine predictions are public and algebraically distinguishable; the frozen reducer applies exact named comparisons with no analyst choices.

power.note: This is a complete deterministic computation on one fixed algebraic instance. No population inference, p-value, confidence interval, or equivalence claim is licensed.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Conservative planning ceiling informed by the earlier standalone prototype and build-time checks; no native degree-study F4 invocation was run before freeze.

primary.name: arithmetic and solver hard controls
primary.definition: Inventory, A/A, planted-solution, unsatisfiable-target, all-solver-complete, subgroup-map, and exact raw-norm identity checks; a failure invalidates comparisons.
primary.source: controls and fixture fields in degree-study.json

primary.name: maximum supplied total degree
primary.definition: Maximum total degree among the equations supplied to F4, before any reduction.

primary.name: semi-regular Hilbert estimate
primary.definition: First non-positive coefficient of prod_i(1-z^d_i)/(1-z)^n using only supplied equation degrees; this exact coefficient calculation is a model estimate, not a certified BFS degree of regularity.

primary.name: affine leading-ideal regularity index
primary.definition: One plus the maximum total degree of a standard monomial of the completed grevlex affine leading ideal; distinct from BFS d_reg of top forms.

primary.name: productive F4 solving degree
primary.definition: Highest F4 step degree that adds a new basis polynomial or one, excluding trailing certification steps.

primary.name: total solving degree
primary.definition: Maximum of supplied input degree and productive F4 solving degree for this procedure.

primary.name: selected F4 pair rows
primary.definition: Sum of pair rows selected across captured native F4 steps; not a sequential Buchberger S-pair count.

primary.name: peak native F4 matrix shape
primary.definition: Maximum rows and maximum columns reported across completed native F4 steps.

primary.name: native F4 field multiplications
primary.definition: Shared f4_fp row-reduction multiplication counter for the one arm; construction, external replay, and report reduction are excluded.

secondary.name: maximum final basis degree
secondary.definition: Maximum total degree of any monomial in the completed interreduced basis.

secondary.name: raw maximum processed degree
secondary.definition: Maximum of supplied input degree and every processed F4 step, including trailing zero-reduction certification steps.

record: CPU model and kernel for replay provenance

stopping_rules.rule: Run the single fixed nine-observation panel once at maximum degree 32, then stop; do not enlarge the factor base, change the fixture, or add an arity after seeing output.
Invalidate every comparison if any observation times out, hits a resource limit, leaves pairs above the degree bound, stops on a staircase, or fails its expected outcome.
Stop before execution if the binary hash, source commit, protocol hash, fixture identity, or checkpoint gate does not match the frozen record.

decision_rule.text: The reducer reports exact tuples and signed deltas only after every hard control passes. Equality claims require field-for-field equality of the preregistered degree tuple. Lower-degree claims require a strictly smaller total_solving_degree and must be shown beside variable, equation, matrix, pair-row, and field-multiplication counts. No single-fixture result licenses population equivalence, scaling, or speedup.
decision_rule.threshold: exact equality for profile claims; nonzero signed delta for presentation effects; strict inequality for lower-degree wording; all hard controls true
decision_rule.statistic: exact per-arm tuple and paired signed difference on the one fixed fixture
decision_rule.interval: none; deterministic exact computation with no sampling inference
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: signed degree, variable, equation, selected-pair-row, matrix-dimension, and field-multiplication differences

inadmissible: running degree-study before this protocol is frozen and committed
bypassing a failed repository checkpoint gate
changing the field, curve, subgroup, relation, factor-base roots, system equations, order, degree bound, or F4 engine after seeing output
quoting local wall or CPU time as a benchmark result
calling selected native F4 pair rows the 249 sequential Buchberger S-pairs from the prior standalone prototype
calling the semi-regular estimate or affine regularity index a certified BFS degree of regularity
treating the degree-two isogeny as a birational coordinate rename or ignoring its kernel and exceptional set
including a Hessian arm on a different curve in the matched-coordinate table
claiming a Curve25519, asymptotic, complete index-calculus, rho, Coppersmith, integer-lifting, or information-theoretic result from this fixture
making a solver-cost claim before external-CAS replay

graphs: input degree and total solving degree by system with selected F4 pair-row labels

invalidation_rules: any hard-control failure invalidates all coordinate comparisons
any incomplete F4 arm invalidates equality or lower-degree wording involving that arm
any binary, commit, protocol, fixture, or analysis-source hash mismatch invalidates the run
external-CAS disagreement blocks every solver-cost interpretation but does not rewrite the retained native output

extensions.execution_unit: One binary invocation emits all nine observations; arm records are conceptual selectors into that matched output, not nine separately timed processes.
extensions.affected_data_status_at_filing: No degree-study invocation through the native shared F4 engine had been run when this protocol was drafted and frozen.
extensions.prior_information: The user supplied results from an earlier standalone graded-lex Buchberger prototype on the same toy fixture. Those values motivate the comparisons but do not count as native F4 observations, A/A evidence, or external replay.
